claims.statement: The built-in browser is an Electron WebContentsView surface owned entirely by the main process (BrowserService in src/main/browser/browser-service.ts) and survives a Renderer reload.

Agent coding permissions never imply browser rights; browser access uses a permission lattice none<read<interact<advanced enforced by BrowserPolicyEngine, with short-lived grants and per-request leases that carry a policyRevision.

Leases expire after a lease TTL (default 15 min) and are all cleared when the policy revision bumps; a stale lease or revision fails with CAPABILITY_LEASE_EXPIRED or POLICY_REVISION_MISMATCH, forcing the agent to refresh.

BrowserAuthorizationCoordinator resolves approvals serially per session, honoring persistent permissions, issuing grantSession for allow-session decisions, applying deny cooldowns, and timing out pending requests after 60s.

BrowserConfirmationManager issues single-use, expiring BrowserConfirmationProofs (default 2 min TTL) bound to a kind and payload digest; sensitive operations require consuming a matching, unconsumed, unexpired proof.

Persistent per-session browser permissions are stored in BrowserPersistentGrantStore (browser-session-grants.json), consulted at request time; runtime grants are held in BrowserService.runtimeGrants for 8h.

BrowserProfileManager manages Session-partition profiles including a default temporary profile, ephemeral profiles, persistent profiles (max 16), and unsafe profiles that are only allowed when advanced mode is enabled.

The advanced browser mode (advancedBrowserMode.enabled, this-launch only) unlocks removing site security headers, disabling web security, allowing insecure content, certificate-bypass domains, and unrestricted raw CDP; turning it off downgrades advanced grants to interact.
Browser header secrets are encrypted with safeStorage and referenced opaquely via secretRef from BrowserSecretVault so the renderer and logs never carry plaintext values.

BrowserService pushes a BrowserCapabilitySnapshot (revision, browserEnabled, automationEnabled, advancedEnabled, sessionPermissions) through a subscription wired to hostManager.setBrowserCapabilitySnapshot, and the Host applies it via browser:init/browser:changed before syncing session browser tools.
On Host stop, BrowserService.onHostStopped clears agent header rules, cancels pending authorizations, revokes all policy grants and lease state, revokes agent tab actions, and clears advanced state.
